rv.q: This version of Antigone , less well-known and certainly less often produced than Sophocles' classic telling of the tale, is the perfect one for these darker times when even truth itself is called into question and it's hard to know the best way to respond to what's going on.
This is a thoughtful, well crafted and resonant work.
The pleasure of watching Jared and Heather Dennis go at each other using Sophocles' sophisticated arguments overcomes any other issues in the production.
This modern adaptation gives the director the choice to put the actors in modern dress.
Rarely have I witnessed such a mood-killing preface to a show, as the director and cast do their best to wring easy laughs out of sublime tragedy.
Despite everyone's best efforts, this Antigone defies relevance.
Carlson’s production transforms a classic tragedy into a timely reflection of the world around us.
I am not one for Greek Tragedies, but found this one to be enjoyable and understandable, and it was nice to see a number of young people in the audience.

cn.t: Promethean's timely production of Anouilh's resistance drama draws clear parallels to contemporary politics, though critics are divided: some praise its powerful relevance and performances, while others cite tonal inconsistencies that undermine its tragic impact.
